sections.title: MADR Decisions & 2-Up Risk Matrix
sections.lede: Architecture Decision Records with explicit context and consequences, paired with a dense 2-up operational risk grid.

blocks.question: How many 64 MiB standby segments should each shard pre-allocate in its warm ring?
context: Multi-tenant storage nodes host up to 64 shards per NVMe volume. On-demand
stalls writers for 14–40 ms under burst rollover, whereas excessive pre-allocation wastes idle disk capacity.
recommendation: so back-to-back burst rollovers never block on extent allocation

alternatives.label: 1 standby segment (64 MiB)
alternatives.summary: Halves idle disk footprint (4 GiB/node), but double-rollover bursts still block on fallocate().

alternatives.label: 2 standby segments (128 MiB)
alternatives.summary: Absorbs double-rollover bursts with zero append-path stalls at a bounded 8 GiB/node reservation.

alternatives.label: 4 standby segments (256 MiB)
alternatives.summary: Reserves 16 GiB/node with negligible p99 gain over a 2-segment ring.

consequences: Reserves 8 GiB of pre-allocated NVMe space per 64-shard storage node.
Removes filesystem allocator locks from the hot wal_append critical path.

blocks.question: Which checksum algorithm should guard sealed segment frames?
blocks.context: Every frame requires corruption detection at >1 GiB/s scan rates without breaking v1 segment readers.
recommendation: per frame plus SHA-256 over the sealed segment manifest.

alternatives.label: SHA-256 per frame
alternatives.summary: Cryptographic collision resistance, but adds 6× CPU overhead on <256 B frames.

alternatives.label: CRC-32C per frame + SHA-256 per manifest
alternatives.summary: Single-cycle ARM64/x86_64 CRC instruction path with cryptographic manifest sealing.

alternatives.label: xxHash64 per frame
alternatives.summary: Fast non-cryptographic hash, but breaks v1 wire compatibility.

consequences: Preserves zero-downtime rolling upgrades alongside v1 segment readers.
Detects bit-rot at line rate while manifest SHA-256 seals whole-segment identity.

blocks.title: Stuck reader cursor pins retired mmap segments
mitigation: Enforce a 30 s reader lease TTL; expired cursors clone remaining unread bytes to a bounded heap buffer and release their mmap pin

blocks.title: Container hits Linux vm.max_map_count ceiling
mitigation: and caps mapped segments at 512 per process.

blocks.title: APFS F_FULLFSYNC latency spikes on developer laptops
mitigation: NAND flush executes once per 64 MiB seal rather than per frame, bounding amortized cost below 2 ms

blocks.title: Torn tail frame after ungraceful host power loss
mitigation: Startup recovery truncates trailing frames failing CRC-32C verification before opening writer cursors
